newsitem.title: USA: Russia sees commercial debt restructured by yr-end.
newsitem.headline: Russia sees commercial debt restructured by yr-end.

text.p: Russian Central Bank Chairman Sergei Dubinin said Saturday the rescheduling of Russia's commercial debt with foreign creditors should be completed by the end of the year.
"I hope we will finish this rescheduling before the end of the year," he told reporters after talks with Group of Seven (G7) finance ministers.
Dubinin described the talks as "almost routine" but very important for Russia.

Commenting on the health of Russian President Boris Yeltsin, Dubinin said there had been no crisis for the economy, adding that intervention in the currency market in August had been less than $1.0 billion.
First Deputy Prime Minister Valdimir Potanin told reporters no difficult questions had arisen. "The discussion was of a more general character," he said.

"They asked a lot of questions about restructuring reforms in our economy, about targets of economic and financial policy for next year and about the budget for next year. It was very positive," he added.

Asked if the health of President Boris Yeltsin, who is awaiting heart surgery had been discussed, Potanin said, "Since the problem has been made public and been discussed openly, it has lost its acuteness and the situation is quite calm."

The IMF loan, agreed earlier this year, is subject to strict monthoy monitoring. A tranche of about $330 million was delayed in July over concern over the level of tax revenues. The IMF and Moscow agreed new slightly easier performance targets and the tranche was paid but economist say Russia's ability to collect the necessary revenue will remain a key concern.
The 1997 draft budget foresees a deficit of 3.3 percent of GDP and economists says Russia's ability to collect the necessary revenue will remain a key concern.
